engagement_summary: Primary ask: Dedicated capacity for customer-facing chat + embeddings with bursty e-commerce traffic and strict P95 latency targets.
Workloads: real-time support agent (chat), semantic search (embeddings), in-band reranking for recommendation pipelines.
Baseline constraints: steady-state QPS ~45 requests/sec; average payload ~420 tokens/request; avg tokens generated ~300 tokens/request.
Peak behavior: expected flash sale bursts up to 250 QPS for 3-7 minute windows; planning must support 30x short-term burst multiplier.
Latency targets: interactive P95 <= 250ms for short-form chat (<=128 tokens), P95 <= 1s for long-form summarization; 99th percentile fallbacks defined.
Throughput guarantees requested: committed baseline throughput with burst headroom and SLA credit if sustained throttling occurs above commitment.
Throughput planning metric: tokens/sec steady-state ~22k TPS; peak tokens/sec during bursts ~150k TPS (planning envelope used for GPU reservation sizing).
Model preferences: open model family (LLM-XL variant) with quantized variant available; preference to route to smaller quantized fallback for cold starts.
Routing/fallback needs: multi-tier routing (primary high-perf, quantized fallback, cross-region fallback), automated fallback on queueing and latency spikes.
Security/compliance: VPC deployment with KMS integration, audit logs persisted for 7 years (legal asks for 10-year retention for certain data), SSO via SAML enforced.
Proposed reserved config: initial reservation proposal = 8 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (or equivalent mixed pool), autoscale policy for burst to +50% with billing cap.
SLA negotiation points: target uptime 99.95, latency SLOs per route, credits for missed latency SLOs, data residency clause for EU traffic.
Cost sensitivity: medium-high; willing to commit annual ARR for lower unit cost but requires clear breakpoints where quantized routing reduces token cost by >=25%.
